takeaway: Torsion of the hydatid of Morgagni: sudden testicular pain with a small, very tender lump on the upper pole and a testis in its normal position.

question.text: An 18-year-old footballer has sudden acute pain in his right testicle, no trauma, no fever, a small very tender lump on the upper pole and a normally placed testis. Diagnosis?
question.say: An eighteen-year-old footballer has sudden pain in his right testicle, with no trauma and no fever. There is a small, very tender lump on its upper pole, and the testicle lies normally. What is the likely diagnosis?

answer.say: The answer is torsion of the hydatid of Morgagni.

lines.say: This young footballer is suddenly in pain, with no trauma.

lines.text: Sudden, acute pain in the right testicle.
lines.say: The pain in his right testicle came on suddenly.

lines.text: The testicle sits in a normal position.
lines.say: The testicle sits in its normal position.

lines.text: A small, very tender lump on the upper pole.
lines.say: On its upper pole sits a small, very tender lump.

lines.text: The appendix testis: a Mullerian duct remnant.
lines.say: (laugh) Meet the blue appendix testis, or hydatid of Morgagni: a Mullerian duct remnant at the top of the testis, now twisted.

lines.text: It is like the fimbriated end of the fallopian tube.
lines.say: It is comparable to the fimbriated end of the fallopian tube in females.

lines.text: Remember: a tender upper pole lump with a normal testis is torsion of the hydatid of Morgagni.
lines.say: Remember: a tender upper pole lump with a normal testis is torsion of the hydatid of Morgagni.
